title: SQ-triggered upgrade funnel with decaying onboarding credits
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: We will test whether linking enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) activity to a tailored onboarding credit schedule and upgrade messaging increases PLG->sales conversion for customers showing enterprise intent. Background: Sales and SE teams report that early SQ submission is a strong indicator of intent to buy Dedicated/Private, but current self-serve credits and expirations are uniform and can either expire too quickly for security evals or be overly generous for low-intent users. Hypothesis: If we (a) detect SQ submission or download, (b) automatically adjust that account's onboarding credit decay to a slower curve and increase targeted in-product upgrade prompts + playbook outreach, conversion to paid Dedicated/Private within 90 days will increase by >= 20% without materially increasing credit abuse. Metrics: Primary: % of SQ accounts that create paid commitment (Reserved/Dedicated or Private license) within 90 days. Secondary: activation (first 1M tokens used), MRR influenced, credits burned per account, abuse indicators (multi-account usage, sudden spike from new accounts). Design of experiment: 1) Trigger detection: mark accounts when they either (i) submit a security questionnaire form via the Guardrails page, (ii) download the enterprise SQ PDF, or (iii) request an enterprise trial via Contact Sales form. 2) Treatment variants (A/B/C): A - Control (current 60-day flat credit expiry); B - Extended tail: credits expire after 90 days but slow decay after 30 days (linear-to-exponential decay); C - Conditional uplift: immediate +30% credit top-up and 120-day expiry but with enterprise flag and manual sales/SE outreach queue. 3) Messaging: in-product banner + contextual help center card + automated follow-up email thread templated for SE. 4) Instrumentation: tag accounts with sq_triggered=true, treatment_group=(control|tail|uplift), capture events: sq_submitted, sq_downloaded, contact_sales, credit_topup, credit_expired, first_paid_commit, dedicated_request, private_deploy_request. Data stored in analytics with cohort windows at 30/60/90 days. Experiment length: 10 weeks with interim look at 4 weeks for safety. Acceptance criteria: uplift >= 20% in paid conversion at 90 days for any treatment with no >15% increase in abuse signals or >10% increase in net credit cost per converted account. Rollout plan: start with accounts with company_size >=50 and org_email domain matching company domain to reduce noise, then expand. Engineering asks: lightweight tag + credit policy engine rule, ability to set per-account expiry curve, event instrumentation. Design asks: updated banner, SE playbook doc, and email templates. Legal asks: ensure SQ data is stored per compliance norms; Sales/SE requested an opt-out toggle. Risk & mitigations: Abuse risk mitigated by enterprise domain verification + manual review queue for uplift group. Billing complexity mitigated by only applying credits to new trial buckets; non-billable unit labeling for accounting. Next steps: design review, engineering spike for per-account expiry, legal sign-off on SQ-derived UX, run pilot with 250 qualifying accounts.

decisions: Use three variant arms (control, extended tail, conditional uplift) to separate effects of extended expiry vs explicit top-up+SE outreach.
Eligibility restricted to verified company domains and org_size >= 50 for initial pilot to reduce noise and mitigate abuse.
Uplift top-up capped at +30% after engineering and finance review to limit credit budget risk.
